title: Adaptive OTEL exporter router for redundant tracing backends
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Build a resilient, configurable routing layer in the OpenTelemetry exporter stack that can direct spans to multiple tracing backends (Tempo primary, Jaeger secondary) with per-tenant routing rules, dynamic sampling, and graceful fallback. Motivation: current uni-directional OTEL wiring is brittle during region outages and makes it hard to onboard new backends or split traffic for experiments. This ticket implements a pluggable router component inside the runtime's tracing hooks, enforced policies for header-based routing, and observability to verify correct delivery.
acceptance_criteria: Router component can route spans to two backends concurrently (primary + fallback) with configurable split ratios
Header-based routing: x-redwood-routing and tenant metadata can pin traces to a specific backend
Dynamic sampling adjustments applied before exporter serialization
On exporter failure, spans are retried to fallback backend without blocking request path
Relevant latency/error metrics show exporter success/failure per backend and are visible in Console dashboards
E2E integration tests for Tempo and Jaeger pipelines pass in CI
Rollout can be toggled via Console feature flag and deployed via canary
updates: 2025-02-20 - Ticket created by Asha: initial scope and design questions documented. Identified need for per-tenant routing and non-blocking fallback.

2025-02-24 - Design review with Observability and Runtime teams. Decided on in-process router vs sidecar: in-process preferred to reduce cross-network tail latency. Action: prototype router as middleware in the OTEL span exporter path.

2025-02-28 - Prototype implemented: basic router selects backend by header or tenant map; added async buffer to avoid backpressure on request threads. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/runtime/pull/4123

2025-03-01 - Load test (k6) of prototype: exporter CPU increase ~8% at p95 throughput, memory +30MB for async buffer. Observability team recommends limiting buffer size and exposing backpressure metrics.

2025-03-03 - Added metrics: exporter_outcome{backend}, exporter_latency_ms{backend}, exporter_buffer_depth, exporter_retry_count. Dashboard draft: Console -> Observability -> Tracing -> Exporter Health. Link to dashboard spec: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-dashboard-spec

2025-03-04 - Security review kickoff: verified no PII escaping, routing decisions operate on tenant-id and sampling headers only. Security asked for opt-in audit log flag for tenant routing changes. Added follow-up task.
2025-03-04 - Blocking item: Jaeger client in runtime uses legacy protobuf mapping that requires a small adapter. Created subtask ENG-8439 to implement jaeger adapter
testing_plan: Unit tests for router decision logic and adapter normalization. Integration tests exercising header-based routing and fallback in a dockerized Tempo+Jaeger environment. CI job will run a synthetic trace workload and assert span counts landed in expected backend endpoints. Add canary pipeline to route 5% of prod sampling to new router for 24h and validate metrics and error rates.
rollback_plan: Feature gated by runtime flag. If exporter error rate or exporter_buffer_depth exceeds thresholds (configurable), auto-disable router and revert to single-exporter mode. Can also toggle off via Console feature flag to revert traffic instantly. Postmortem + hotfix PR to remove router code if critical.
risks_mitigation: Risk: added latency due to routing and buffering. Mitigation: keep synchronous path minimal (decision only), perform export write asynchronously; enforce strict max buffer size; emit exporter_latency_ms to detect regressions. Risk: divergence in span formats between Tempo and Jaeger. Mitigation: normalization adapters per backend, tests across span attributes and baggage propagation.
next_steps: Finish jaeger adapter (ENG-8439), add audit logging toggle, wire Console feature flag, run canary in staging with 5% of traces, iterate on buffer sizing based on real traffic, and ship in console-2025.03 if metrics stable for 48h. Notify partner teams (Platform, Security, SRE) before canary.
notes_for_review: Solicit feedback on: 1) acceptable default split ratio (we propose primary=100% with fallback on failure), 2) buffer sizing trade-offs (defaults: 1000 spans, max age 5s), 3) what tenant metadata keys should be trusted for routing. Please review prototype PR and load test artifacts linked above.
